sentences.text: The definite case of the petitioners is that the property bearing Sy. No.1 (1A Block 20)9 of Jakkur Plantation village, Yelahanka Hobli, BBMP Khatha No. 467/1A Block 20 and 9 coming within the limits of BBMP measuring 1250 Sq. Meters has been acquired under Gazette notification No. S.O. No.1874 (E) dated 30.07.2010.
Prior to that Preliminary Notification issued under S.O. No.3159(E) dated 09.12.2009.
Subsequently the respondent No.2/LAO has awarded a total sum of Rs.3,89,28,571/- as compensation for 1618 Sq. feet of the land belongs to the petitioners.
The petitioners received the same under protest and filed an application for enhancing the compensation.
Accordingly, the said application taken by the respondent No. 3 for consideration.
.3. In the said petition, the respondent No.2 filed statement of objection stating that the contention urged by the petitioner are baseless and the same are made without any substance.
The petitioner has not produced any relevant documents to justify his claim for enhanced A.P. No.194/2021 compensation and the claim of the petitioner cannot be sustained in law.
Hence, question of enhancement of compensation will not arise and the claim of the petitioner is liable to be dismissed by the respondent No.2.

The claimants have not produced any cogent evidence to establish that they are entitled to higher compensation than what has been awarded by the respondent No. 1 in this case, hence, the claim is liable to be rejected in limine.
Accordingly, prayed to dismiss the reference.
. 4 . T h e r e a f t e r , t h e A r b i t r a t o r h o l d a n i n q u i r y a n d p a s s e d c o m m o n o r d e r i n LAQ/ARB/NH-7/CR-99/2012- 13 dated 12.02.2021.

.5. Being aggrieved by the impugned Arbitral Award, the petitioner filed this petition under Section 34(2) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, setting up the following :

2 :GROUNDS:
The petitioners claim that the amount fixed by the respondent No.2 was unfair and the respondent No. 1 while enhancing the compensation have not taken into A.P.
No.194/2021 consideration about the market value and the other necessary facts determine the fair compensation.

The award passed by the respondent No.2 by fixing Rs.3,606/- per Sq. feet is unjust and against to the provisions of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 and among other grounds, prayed for reconsidering the impugned award and also alternative prayer to remand the matter to the Arbitrator for fresh consideration.
.6.

sentences.text: The respondent No.2 and 3 filed a detailed objections claiming that the application is not maintainable either in law or on facts and the respondent No. 3 passed the award as per the guidance value produced before the Arbitrator pertaining to the year 2011.
The petitioner is attempting to mislead this Court by drawing reference to incorrect/wholly inapplicable guidance notification.
The respondent No.1 totally denied all the grounds claimed by the petitioner in the petition.

The Arbitrator/ respondent No. 3 passed the award after giving full opportunity of hearing to the petitioner by considering the material evidence on record for enhancement of compensation together with all other statutory benefits available under the LA Act in accordance with law and prayed for dismissal of the petition.
.7. The respondent No.1 appeared before the Court through DGP.
The respondents No.2 and 3 appeared before the Court through their Advocate.
The entire records in LAQ/ARB/NH-7/CR/99/2012-13 dated 12.02.2021 secured from the Arbitrator.

.8. On the basis of above, the points for consideration are as under:
1) Whether the impugned award of the Arbitrator/SLAO is against law, fact, evidence and probabilities of the case and liable to be intervened by this Court?
2) What order or award?
A.P. No.194/2021 .9.
Heard the arguments.

Perused the materials on record, on that basis my findings on the above points are as under:
Point No.1 : In the negative Point No.2 : As per final order, for the following:
REASONS .10.
POINT No.1:
Before proceeding further in this case, it is relevant to note an admitted and undisputed facts in this case.

sentences.text: It is also an admitted and undisputed fact in this case that the respondent No.2/Special Land Acquisition and A.P. No.194/2021 Competent Authority of National Highways Authority of India being a SLAO determined the compensation at Rs. 1,618/- per Sq. feet for the acquired land for BDA/BMRDA sites.

sentences.text:
It is also admitted and undisputed fact that a sum of Rs.40,08,164/- to the land, Rs.
1,95,952/- towards building and Rs. 1,01,187/- towards trees, was disbursed to the petitioners as compensation.
.11.

Subsequent to the receipt of compensation or passing of the award, the petitioners filed an application before the respondent No.3 claiming that they are entitled for enhancement of compensation claiming that the land would fetch more than Rs. 6,500/- per Sq. feet as on 14.09.2010.
On basis of the said application, the respondent No.3 hold an inquiry and passed common order in LAQ/ARB/NH-7/CR-99/2012-13 dated 12.02.2021.
The respondent No.3 in its order enhanced the compensation at Rs3,606/- per Sq. feet.

As per petition averment at para No. 7,
the respondent No. 3 / LAO / project director has fixed the compensation at Rs. 1,618/- per Sq. feet and that has been enhanced by the A.P. No.194/2021 Arbitrator / Special Deputy Commissioner /
respondent No. 1 by adding Rs.3,606/- per Sq. feet.
if this pleading is accepted, then it has to be accepted that the respondent No. 1/ Arbitrator fixed compensation at Rs. 5,224/- per Sq. feet.

Further at this juncture, it is relevant to note that as per petition averments, the petitioner claims that the compensation fixed by respondent No.1 is Rs.40,08,164/- for acquired land, Rs. 1,95,952/-
towards building and Rs. 1,01,187/- towards trees etc., and that has been enhanced to the tune of Rs.
4,85,00,700/-.

Of course the petitioners claimed that the market value of the acquired land is more than Rs. 6,500/- per Sq. feet, but no documents have been placed before the court to substantiate the said contention.
The materiel on record sufficiently shows that the Arbitrator constrained all the material before it, properly assess the market value as per the order.

When the petitioner fails to make out any ground to show that the award passed by the Arbitrator is arbitrary or against the provision of law, certainly such order cannot be interfered by this A.P. No.194/2021 Court.

Therefore, this Court is of the humble opinion that the petitioner has failed to make out sufficient grounds to intervene with the order passed by the respondent No.1 and the order of the respondent no.1 is in accordance with the law and said order is in accordance with law by considering all the material documents placed before the Arbitrator.
Accordingly, the point No.2 is held in the negative.
.12. Point No.2:
In view of my above finding, I proceed to pass the following.
ORDER Petition filed under Section 34 of Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 by the petitioner is hereby dismissed.
